title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: ½-simplicial (semi-simplicial: face maps only) k-modules L. with finite free components, studied for a dévissage of '∂-perfect' semi-simplicial complexes and of exterior powers. From the previous and next pages, the standard building blocks are Λ^iℒ (ranks C(n+1,i), acyclic for i≥1) and Λ^jΨ (ranks C(n,j), homology of rank 1 in degree j). Here ℒ_n ≅ k^{n+1} has face maps deleting coordinates, and Ψ is the rank-n augmentation-type kernel. A '(très) spécial' L. is one isomorphic to ⊕_{i≥1} Λ^iℒ⊗M_i ⊕ ⊕_{j≥0} Λ^jΨ⊗N_j with M_i, N_j free of ranks μ_i, ν_j.

Top of page (inside a bracketed proof). This closes step 2° of a proof that exterior powers Λ^k of special objects are special. One is reduced to showing that Λ^k(Λ^hΨ_{-h}) and Λ^k(Λ^hΨ_{+h}) are special ('even very special'). Their components are visibly free. Since Λ^hΨ_{-h} is homotopic to 0, the H_i of its exterior powers vanish; the rest is a garbled statement about ranks being polynomial in n.

Remark (main content). A very special L. is determined up to isomorphism by two pieces of data: its rank function f_L(n) = rg L_n and the homology ranks ν_j = rg H_j(L.) = rg N_j. The proof writes Σ_{i≥1} μ_i C(n+1,i) = f_L(n) − Σ_j ν_j C(n,j). Equivalently, with P_i(n) = C(n,i), f_L(n−1) − Σ_j ν_j P_j(n−1) = Σ_{i≥1} μ_i P_i(n). The binomial polynomials P_i form a Z-basis of the integer-valued polynomials, so knowing this polynomial for large n determines the μ_i.

Next page. Existence criterion: given ν_j ≥ 0 and an integer-valued polynomial f, write g = f − Σν_jP_j = Σ_{i≥0} μ_i C(n+1,i). A very special L. with these invariants exists iff μ_0 = 0 and μ_i ≥ 0 for i ≥ 1. Moreover μ_0 = g(−1), so μ_0 = 0 ⇔ f(−1) = Σ(−1)^j ν_j = χ.

Purpose: a numerical classification (rank polynomial plus Betti numbers) of the 'normal forms' into which ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and their exterior/multiplicative constructions are dévissé'd.
errors: Proof sketch at top is incomplete/garbled: from Λ^hΨ_{-h} homotopic to 0 one gets vanishing homology of its exterior powers only via a Dold–Puppe-type argument (exterior powers preserve homotopy for semi-simplicial modules), which is not stated.
The family P_i, i≥1, alone is not a basis of integer-valued polynomials (P_0 is missing); it is only a free family. That suffices for uniqueness, and the next page correctly uses i≥0.
Identifying ν_j with rg H_j tacitly requires H_j free (e.g. k a field or the N_j free), and rank determination requires k with well-defined rank (k ≠ 0 commutative).

ideas.what: Very special semi-simplicial modules as direct sums of exterior powers of standard objects ℒ, Ψ tensored with free modules; classification up to isomorphism by the rank polynomial plus Betti numbers
ideas.modern_name: normal form/classification of semi-simplicial (Δ_inj) modules of polynomial growth; representations of FI-type categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related to later work on FI-modules and polynomial functors (Church–Ellenberg–Farb 2010s), but not this exact statement

ideas.what: Uniqueness of multiplicities via the Z-basis of binomial polynomials C(n,i) for integer-valued polynomials
Evaluation of the rank polynomial at n = −1 equals the Euler characteristic of homology (f(−1) = Σ(−1)^j ν_j), as a necessary existence condition
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial reciprocity/Euler characteristic as value at −1 (Ehrhart–Macdonald–Stanley type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stanley/Macdonald for reciprocity in combinatorics; unsure for semi-simplicial modules

ideas.what: Exterior powers of contractible semi-simplicial modules remain acyclic, used to show Λ^k of special objects is special
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Puppe homotopy invariance of non-additive functors

missed.claim: A complete numerical classification of 'very special' semi-simplicial free modules. They are determined up to isomorphism by the rank function and the homology ranks. They exist iff the binomial-coordinate multiplicities are nonnegative and the Euler-characteristic condition f(−1) = χ holds. This is a small structure theorem for semi-simplicial modules of polynomial growth that I do not know in the literature.
missed.quote: Soit L. k-module ½ simplicial très spécial, alors L. est connu à isom. près ... quand on connaît la n ↦ rg_k L_n = f_L(n) ... et les rg_k H_j(L.)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It parallels FI-module/representation-stability results where character polynomials and polynomial growth of dimensions are central. The f(−1) = χ condition is a reciprocity statement of the kind studied in FI/Δ_inj-module theory.

missed.claim: The rank polynomial evaluated at −1 gives the Euler characteristic of the homology. This links polynomial growth of semi-simplicial modules to combinatorial reciprocity.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is analogous to reciprocity phenomena (Ehrhart, Stanley) and to 'regularized' Euler characteristics of infinite complexes. It could be checked against modern work on semi-simplicial/FI-modules.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, apparently unpublished classification of very special semi-simplicial modules by rank polynomial plus Betti numbers, with an f(−1) = χ criterion on the next page. The mathematics is elementary and the setting idiosyncratic, so it is a notable but minor unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: First line is probably 'Λ^k(Λ^hΨ_{-h}) et Λ^k(Λ^hΨ_{+h}) sont spéciaux': the outer exterior power on the second term looks like the same Λ^k, not Λ^h.
'rg_k H_j(L.)' may read 'rg_k π_j(L.)' (homotopy = homology of the semi-simplicial module), matching the next page's notation.
The inserted phrase above 'à coefficients entiers' is likely '(à valeurs entières)', correcting coefficients to integer-valued polynomials.
